title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typescript page, not a handwritten note. It is page 152 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I, Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §12.3, which computes the maximal torus of Pic^0 of a curve. It has been filed among the 1976 de Rham notes, and its archive stamp is 470.

Setup: C is a proper curve over a field k, π: C̃ → C is its normalization, and C̃ is a disjoint union of smooth curves.

The argument:
1. Pic^0_{C̃/k} has reductive rank 0, since it is an abelian variety (or a unipotent extension of one). So the maximal torus of Pic^0_{C/k} lies in N = Ker(Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{C̃/k}).
2. From the sequence 0 → O_C^* → π_*O_{C̃}^* → Q → 0 (via EGA IV 21.8.5), N is an extension of a torus T by a connected unipotent group U, which has a composition series with G_a quotients.
3. Let T' be the maximal torus of N. Then T'∩U is both unipotent and multiplicative, hence trivial (SGA 3 XVII 2.4). T' surjects onto T (SGA 3 XII 7.1 e). So T' ≅ T canonically.
4. To make T explicit, take k separably closed. Let J be the set of components of C̃. For each x let J(x) be the set of branches of C at x, i.e. the points of C̃ over x. Define R(x) = Z^{J(x)}/Z (diagonal) and R = (⊕_x R_x)/Im Z^J.

Modern reading: form the bipartite dual graph Γ, whose vertices are the components and the singular points and whose edges are the branches. Then R = coker(Z^V → Z^E) = H^1(Γ, Z), which is torsion-free. The torus is T = G_m^E/G_m^V = R ⊗ G_m, so R is its cocharacter group. Its rank is Σ_x(|J(x)|−1) − |J| + (number of connected components), the classical toric rank.

Purpose: this feeds the semistable-reduction and monodromy analysis of SGA 7 IX, where the toric part of the special fibre of the Néron model is described via the dual graph.
errors: The last sentence reads 'tore maximal de N, donc de Pic^o_{X/k}'. In context this should be Pic^o_{C/k}, either a typo in the typescript or local notation from SGA 7 IX.
The notation switches between R(x) in (12.3.1) and R_x in (12.3.2); this is purely notational.
No mathematical errors. The claim that T' → T is an isomorphism is correctly justified by the two SGA 3 references.

ideas.what: The maximal torus of Pic^0 of a singular curve lies in the kernel of pullback to the normalization, and is identified with the torus quotient of that kernel.
ideas.modern_name: Toric part of the generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht/Serre structure of Pic^0 of a singular curve)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht and Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes), in the scheme setting Grothendieck in SGA 7

ideas.what: Description of the torus via branches: R = (⊕_x Z^{J(x)}/Z)/Z^J, i.e. the cocharacter group as H^1 of the dual graph.
ideas.modern_name: Toric rank = first Betti number of the dual graph; character/cocharacter group H_1/H^1(Γ,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX; later Raynaud and the tropical-geometry literature

ideas.what: A torus intersects a unipotent group trivially, and a maximal torus surjects onto the torus quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Standard structure theory of commutative algebraic groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of SGA 7 IX §12.3, published in 1972, apparently a stray sheet filed among the 1976 notes. The content is standard and fully published.
transcription_corrections: The page header reads '- 152 -' and 'IX', identifying it as SGA 7 Exposé IX, page 152. These lines are absent from the machine transcription.
The typescript reads 'au-dessus' with a typing irregularity ('au-deseus'), not a different word.
(12.3.2) is R = (⊕_x R_x)/Im Z^J, with the subscript x under ⊕, as transcribed.
